template_name: Memory Reconsolidation in Architectural Spatial Context
calibration_constraint: Bridge warrants ≤ CAPACITY (0.45) per pre-panel review

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant navigates familiar spatial environment, reactivating stored hippocampal cognitive map (place cell ensemble corresponding to the learned layout)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Hippocampal CA1/CA3 place cells; grid cells in entorhinal cortex

data.finding: Place cells in hippocampus fire at specific locations in learned environments; returning to environment reactivates same place cell ensemble
data.effect: Spatial memory stored in place cell ensemble

data.finding: Memory reactivation is necessary for reconsolidation; passive presence in environment without active navigation may not trigger reactivation

justification.backing: O'Keefe's place cell discovery established that spatial environments are represented by specific hippocampal cell ensembles. Returning to a familiar environment reactivates this ensemble, which is the precondition for reconsolidation.
justification.qualifier: Place cell reactivation is demonstrated in rodents; human evidence relies on fMRI pattern reinstatement which is a less direct measure of place cell activity.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human spatial memory does not rely on place cell-like representations; but fMRI evidence supports hippocampal spatial pattern encoding in humans.

mechanism_chain.process: Reactivated spatial memory enters labile state requiring protein synthesis (NMDA-receptor-dependent, Zif268 expression) for restabilization; reconsolidation window opens (~4–6 hours in animal models)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Basolateral amygdala → hippocampal CA1; protein synthesis-dependent restabilization

data.finding: Protein synthesis inhibitors administered after memory reactivation disrupt subsequently reconsolidated memory; memory becomes labile after retrieval
Reconsolidation window in rodents is ~4-6 hours; blocking protein synthesis outside this window does not impair memory

justification.backing: Nader's reconsolidation discovery showed that retrieved memories become temporarily labile and require protein synthesis for restabilization. This molecular mechanism is well-established in animal models.
justification.qualifier: The 4-6 hour window is established in rodent fear conditioning. Human spatial reconsolidation windows are untested; they may differ in duration.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human memory reconsolidation operates differently or has a different temporal window than animal models; human evidence is indirect.

mechanism_chain.process: During reconsolidation window, new spatial information (architectural modifications) can be integrated into the existing cognitive map, updating rather than replacing the stored representation

data.finding: New information presented during reconsolidation window can be integrated into the reactivated memory
Integration rather than replacement: new information is assimilated into existing memory structure during reconsolidation

justification.backing: Reconsolidation provides a mechanism for memory updating: during the labile window, new information can be integrated into the existing memory trace rather than creating a competing trace.
justification.qualifier: ANALOGICAL warrant: the application to spatial/architectural modification is inferred from general reconsolidation research. No studies have tested reconsolidation during building renovation.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial memory reconsolidation operates differently from episodic memory reconsolidation; or if the modification magnitude exceeds integration capacity.

mechanism_chain.process: If spatial modification is too large (exceeds schema-updating capacity), reconsolidation fails: old map is destabilized but new map cannot integrate, producing spatial disorientation

data.finding: Reconsolidation has boundary conditions: if new information is too discrepant from the original memory, reconsolidation fails and disorientation may result
The ~30% modification threshold is estimated from schema-updating capacity research; not empirically tested for spatial layouts

justification.backing: Reconsolidation is not unlimited: there are boundary conditions beyond which the updating mechanism fails. For spatial memory, modifications that exceed the schema-updating capacity may destabilize the old map without successful integration of the new layout.
justification.qualifier: The 30% threshold is a panel estimate based on analogy to other reconsolidation boundary conditions. Direct testing in architectural contexts is absent.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial reconsolidation has different boundary conditions than other memory types; or if occupants simply form new maps rather than updating old ones after large changes.

hippocampal_encoding.interpretation: Time window during which reactivated spatial memory is labile and can be updated by new spatial information
hippocampal_encoding.note: Established in animal fear conditioning; human spatial reconsolidation window untested

arousal_level.interpretation: Reconsolidation requires explicit reactivation of the stored memory; passive presence in a familiar environment may not suffice

spatial_configuration.interpretation: Modifications affecting ≤30% of spatial layout can be integrated via reconsolidation; >30% exceeds schema-updating capacity and produces disorientation

age_group.effect: Reconsolidation capacity may be reduced; older adults show weaker reconsolidation effects in lab paradigms

anxiety_trait.effect: Anxiety-related hyperactivation of amygdala may accelerate reconsolidation destabilization but impair integration of new spatial information

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget deficit during reconsolidation window may impair protein synthesis-dependent restabilization, potentially leaving spatial memories in a destabilized state. This interaction is speculative (confidence 0.25) but clinically relevant for hospital renovation contexts where patients are already in allostatic deficit.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Low perceived control during spatial environment changes elevates stress, which modulates reconsolidation via glucocorticoid effects on hippocampal protein synthesis. The direction is complex: moderate stress enhances reconsolidation; high stress may impair it (Schwabe & Wolf, 2010).

cross_template_references: ED_SCHEMA_ENCODING_001 — schema availability modulates reconsolidation integration capacity
ED_HIPPOCAMPAL_ENCODING_001 — initial encoding strength determines reconsolidation susceptibility
STRESS-I T6 — cortisol modulates protein synthesis during reconsolidation

spatial_configuration.interpretation: Larger spatial modifications during reconsolidation window may produce more disorientation if they exceed integration capacity; predicted monotonic but no empirical dose-response data

environmental_novelty_level.interpretation: Preserving ≥2 recognizable landmarks during renovation supports reactivation and reconsolidation-based updating rather than disorientation
